key_insight: DxToniaNet estimated leg dystonia severity in children with cerebral palsy from clinical videos; this study concerns movement assessment, not cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Automated video scoring could support more objective severity measurement in care and clinical trials, pending further validation.
method: OpenPose tracked bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates during a seated hand open-close task.
Normalized coordinates yielded 69 movement variance and amplitude features.
A neural network estimated expert-rated Global Dystonia Rating Scale leg scores.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed recordings from 298 children across two centers, using dystonia-positive videos for development and testing; five-fold validation preceded independent-center testing, with reported MAE of 1.71 points and 90–94% accuracy distinguishing videos more than 4 points apart.
watch_item: Retrospective evaluation restricted to dystonia-positive videos does not establish performance for screening or prospective clinical use.
paper_title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
